env: A Harbor-hosted 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell environment (`{{platform}}`) with Docker, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, and NGC access to `nvcr.io/nvstaging/vss-core/vss-rt-cv` plus `nvstaging/vss-warehouse/vss-warehouse-app-data`. The VSS repository is checked out at `{{repo_root}}`, and the build skill writes to a fresh self-contained build directory under `{{repo_root}}/_builds/rt-cv-person-detection-rtdetr-harbor/` (or the next suffixed collision-resolved folder). This is a generation-focused eval using the same Harbor hardware setup as the upstream Harbor eval: the generated output must stay self-contained under `_builds/`, must not modify upstream compose files under `deploy/docker/`, and must prepare the RT-CV detection/tracking deployment with the same warehouse video sets. RT-CV bounding-box metadata must be published to Kafka and stored in Elasticsearch through the shared ELK path. The RT-CV service key for this eval is the selected integration contract's `perception-2d-fusion`; `perception-2d` and `perception-alerts` are not acceptable substitutes.

expects.query: Use the `/vss-build-vision-agent` skill to generate an RT-CV detection/tracking deployment on Harbor for `{{platform}}` from `{{repo_root}}`. Submit this exact prompt to the skill: "Create a profile for generating bounding box cv metadata (object detection and tracking) of persons using RT-DETR. Use the same warehouse video sets. Publish streamed detection metadata to Kafka, store it in Elasticsearch, and expose the RT-CV API for health and metrics. Preserve exact service keys from the selected integration contracts rather than substituting similar services from another profile. Include a compact RT-CV Metadata Contract section in the manifest that lists the bounding-box metadata fields and the Kafka-to-Elasticsearch path." Choose a new build under `_builds/`, keep the generated output self-contained, and target the Harbor RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell environment.
checks: `{{repo_root}}/_builds/` contains a new Harbor-targeted RT-CV detection/tracking build folder with `compose.yml`, `.env.template`, `MANIFEST.md`, and `allow-list.yml`.
The generated architecture and allow-list resolve to the required components: VIOS + RT-CV + ELK + Kafka.

The generated allow-list includes the RT-CV services contributed by `integrate-vss-detection-tracking-2d.md`, including `perception-2d-fusion`, and does not use `perception-2d` or `perception-alerts` as substitute RT-CV service keys.
The generated output references patched copies under `_builds/<name>/patched/`, not upstream compose files directly.
No upstream compose file under `{{repo_root}}/deploy/docker/` is modified by generation.
The generated manifest or env output targets the Harbor `RTXPRO6000BW` platform with the same 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell hardware shape used by the upstream Harbor eval.

The generated `MANIFEST.md` or generated deploy skill contains a compact `RT-CV Metadata Contract` section that states RT-DETR detection / tracking metadata flows to Kafka and Elasticsearch while using the warehouse sample video set and explicitly lists bounding box coordinates, class labels, confidence, timestamps, sensor IDs, and track IDs.
